It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Khasif related from Mujahid: ﴿Nay, I swear by this city﴾ means: "No" is a rejection of them; "I swear by this city."

Shabib ibn Bishr related from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Nay, I swear by this city﴾ means Makkah, ﴿and you are a freeman in this city﴾. He said: You, O Muhammad, it is lawful for you to fight in it. Similarly it has been related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, Ata, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

Mujahid said: Whatever you kill in it is lawful for you.

Qatadah said: ﴿and you are a freeman in this city﴾: You are in it without hardship or sin.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah made it lawful for him for an hour of a day.

The meaning they have stated has been reported in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon: "Indeed this city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth; so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees may not be cut and its grass may not be uprooted. It was made lawful for me only for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. Let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent." And in another wording [another]: "If anyone takes a concession to fight in it on account of the Messenger of Allah, say: Indeed Allah permitted His Messenger, and He did not permit you." [The hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari, numbers (104, 105, 1832, 4295), and Sahih Muslim, number (1353), from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim related it [Ibn Jarir and] [in A: "Ibn Jarir and"] from the narration of Sharik, who is Ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi, with the same chain.

Ibn Jarir chose that it is general, applying to every begetter and his offspring. This is also a possible meaning.

* *

Al-Kabad: uprightness and straightness. * *

His hadith resembles the hadith of al-Hasan (meaning al-Basri), not the hadith of Anas.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 90, verse 11–20 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn Jarir said: Umar ibn Isma'il ibn Mujalid related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from Atiyyah, from Ibn Umar, concerning His words: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾. He said: "It is a mountain in Hell."

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾ is seventy levels in Hell. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾, he said: "An ascent in Hell." Qatadah said: "It is a severe obstacle, so cross it through obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Qatadah also said, concerning ﴿And what will make you know what the ascent is?﴾, then He informed about crossing it, saying: ﴿It is the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He has not attempted the ascent﴾ means: "Has he not taken the path in which there is salvation and good?" Then He explained it, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the ascent is? It is the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾.

It has been recited as ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ with the genitive construction (idafah), and it has also been recited as a verb (fa-akka raqabatan), in which the subject pronoun is implicit and "al-raqabah" is its object. The meanings of both readings are close to each other.

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ibrahim related to us, Abdullah – meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind – related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, the freedman of the family of al-Zubayr, from Sa'id ibn Marjanah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a believing slave, Allah frees for every limb of his a limb of his from the Fire, to the extent that He frees the hand for the hand, the foot for the foot, and the private part for the private part." Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "Did you hear this from Abu Hurayrah?" Sa'id said: "Yes." So Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a slave of his, the most handsome of his slaves: "Call Mutarraf." When he stood before him, he said: "Go, for you are free for the sake of Allah's Face."

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through several chains, from Sa'id ibn Marjanah, with the same wording. In Muslim's narration, this slave whom Ali ibn al-Husayn, Zayn al-Abidin, freed had been offered ten thousand dirhams for him.

Qatadah said, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Najih, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, Allah will make the redemption of every bone of his a bone of his liberator from the Fire; and any Muslim woman who frees a Muslim woman, Allah will make the redemption of every bone of hers a bone of hers from the Fire."

Ibn Jarir narrated it thus. And this Abu Najih is Amr ibn Abasah al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him.

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh related to us, Baqiyyah related to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd related to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Amr ibn Abasah, that he related to them that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque for the remembrance of Allah in it, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise. Whoever frees a Muslim soul, it will be his ransom from Hell. And whoever grows white hair in Islam, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection."

Another chain: Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us, Hariz related to us, from Sulaym ibn Amir, that Shurahbil ibn al-Simt said to Amr ibn Abasah: "Narrate to us a hadith that contains no addition and no forgetting." Amr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever frees a Muslim slave, it will be his ransom from the Fire, limb for limb. And whoever grows white hair in the way of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever shoots an arrow that reaches the target, whether it hits or misses, it is as if he had freed a slave from the descendants of Isma'il."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated part of it.

Another chain: Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, al-Faraj related to us, Luqman related to us, from Abu Umamah, from Amr ibn Abasah, who said: al-Sulami said: I said to him: "Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that contains no omission and no error." He said: I heard him say: "Whoever has three children born to him in Islam who die before reaching the age of puberty, Allah will admit him to Paradise by the bounty of His mercy towards them. Whoever grows white hair in the way of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah that reaches the enemy, whether it hits or misses, it is for him the reward of freeing a slave. And whoever frees a believing slave, Allah frees for every limb of his a limb of his from the Fire. And whoever spends two spouses (pairs) in the way of Allah, Paradise has eight gates, and Allah will admit him through whichever gate He wills."

These are good, strong chains, and to Allah belongs praise and grace.

Ibn Abbas said: "Its doors are closed." Mujahid said: In the language of Quraysh, "asada al-bab" means he closed the door.

A hadith concerning this will come in the surah: ﴿Woe to every slanderer and mocker﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿sealed shut﴾ means a wall with no door.

Qatadah said: "Mu'sadah" means closed shut, so there is no light in it and no opening, and no exit from it ever, forever.

Abu 'Imran al-Jawni said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will command every tyrant, every devil, and everyone who was feared by people in the world for his evil, to be bound in iron. Then they will be driven to Jahannam, and then the gates will be closed upon them, i.e., sealed shut. He said: "By Allah, their feet will never settle on any resting place. By Allah, they will never look out upon the face of the sky from within it. By Allah, the eyelids of their eyes will never meet in a moment of sleep. By Allah, they will never taste cool drink within it, ever." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

End of the commentary on Surah "al-Balad", and all praise and grace are due to Allah.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 90, verse 11–20 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn Jarir said: Umar ibn Isma'il ibn Mujalid related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from Atiyyah, from Ibn Umar, concerning His words: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾. He said: "It is a mountain in Hell."

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾ is seventy levels in Hell. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿But he has not attempted the ascent﴾, he said: "An ascent in Hell." Qatadah said: "It is a severe obstacle, so cross it through obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Qatadah also said, concerning ﴿And what will make you know what the ascent is?﴾, then He informed about crossing it, saying: ﴿It is the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He has not attempted the ascent﴾ means: "Has he not taken the path in which there is salvation and good?" Then He explained it, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the ascent is? It is the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾.

It has been recited as ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ with the genitive construction (idafah), and it has also been recited as a verb (fa-akka raqabatan), in which the subject pronoun is implicit and "al-raqabah" is its object. The meanings of both readings are close to each other.

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ibrahim related to us, Abdullah – meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind – related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, the freedman of the family of al-Zubayr, from Sa'id ibn Marjanah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a believing slave, Allah frees for every limb of his a limb of his from the Fire, to the extent that He frees the hand for the hand, the foot for the foot, and the private part for the private part." Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "Did you hear this from Abu Hurayrah?" Sa'id said: "Yes." So Ali ibn al-Husayn said to a slave of his, the most handsome of his slaves: "Call Mutarraf." When he stood before him, he said: "Go, for you are free for the sake of Allah's Face."

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through several chains, from Sa'id ibn Marjanah, with the same wording. In Muslim's narration, this slave whom Ali ibn al-Husayn, Zayn al-Abidin, freed had been offered ten thousand dirhams for him.

Qatadah said, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Najih, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, Allah will make the redemption of every bone of his a bone of his liberator from the Fire; and any Muslim woman who frees a Muslim woman, Allah will make the redemption of every bone of hers a bone of hers from the Fire."

Ibn Jarir narrated it thus. And this Abu Najih is Amr ibn Abasah al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him.

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh related to us, Baqiyyah related to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd related to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Amr ibn Abasah, that he related to them that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque for the remembrance of Allah in it, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise. Whoever frees a Muslim soul, it will be his ransom from Hell. And whoever grows white hair in Islam, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection."

Another chain: Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us, Hariz related to us, from Sulaym ibn Amir, that Shurahbil ibn al-Simt said to Amr ibn Abasah: "Narrate to us a hadith that contains no addition and no forgetting." Amr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever frees a Muslim slave, it will be his ransom from the Fire, limb for limb. And whoever grows white hair in the way of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever shoots an arrow that reaches the target, whether it hits or misses, it is as if he had freed a slave from the descendants of Isma'il."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated part of it.

Another chain: Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, al-Faraj related to us, Luqman related to us, from Abu Umamah, from Amr ibn Abasah, who said: al-Sulami said: I said to him: "Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that contains no omission and no error." He said: I heard him say: "Whoever has three children born to him in Islam who die before reaching the age of puberty, Allah will admit him to Paradise by the bounty of His mercy towards them. Whoever grows white hair in the way of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah that reaches the enemy, whether it hits or misses, it is for him the reward of freeing a slave. And whoever frees a believing slave, Allah frees for every limb of his a limb of his from the Fire. And whoever spends two spouses (pairs) in the way of Allah, Paradise has eight gates, and Allah will admit him through whichever gate He wills."

These are good, strong chains, and to Allah belongs praise and grace.

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Ramli related to us, Dhamrah related to us, from Ibn Abi Abalah, from al-Gharif ibn al-Daylami, who said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' and said to him: "Narrate to us a hadith that contains no addition and no omission." He became angry and said: "Indeed one of you reads while his mushaf hangs in his house, and so he adds and omits." We said: "We only wanted a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: We came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning a companion of ours who had made the Fire obligatory for himself by killing, and he said: "Free (a slave) on his behalf, and Allah will free for every limb of his a limb of his from the Fire."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Abi Abalah, from al-Gharif ibn Ayyash al-Daylami, from Wathilah, with the same wording.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad related to us, Hisham related to us, from Qatadah, from Qays al-Judhami, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a Muslim slave, it is his ransom from the Fire." And Abd al-Wahhab al-Khaffaf related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: It is mentioned that Qays al-Judhami narrated from Uqbah ibn Amir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a believing slave, it is her ransom from the Fire."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam and Abu Ahmad both said: Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bajali – from the Banu Bajilah, from the Banu Sulaym – related to us, from Talhah – Abu Ahmad said: Talhah ibn Musarrif related to us – from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awsajah, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed that will admit me to Paradise." He said: "If you have shortened the sermon, you have indeed made the request broad. Free the soul (nasamah) and release the neck (raqabah)." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, are these not one and the same?" He said: "No. Freeing the soul is that you alone free it, and releasing the neck is that you help in its freeing. And the generous gift of milk-animal, and shelter for a kinsman who is an wrongdoer. If you cannot do that, then feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, enjoin what is good, forbid what is evil, and if you cannot do that, then restrain your tongue except from good."

* *

As for His words: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾, Ibn Abbas said: "On a day of famine." Likewise said Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others. Al-saghab is hunger.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "On a day when food is precious."

Qatadah said: "On a day when food is desired."

* *

As for His words: ﴿an orphan﴾, meaning: feed on such a day an orphan, ﴿having ties of kinship﴾, meaning: a relative of his. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Yazid related to us, Hisham informed us, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Sulayman ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Charity to the poor is a (single) charity, and to a kinsman it is two: charity and maintaining ties of kinship."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, and this is a sound chain.

* *

As for His words: ﴿or a needy person in distress﴾, meaning: a poor man lying prostrate, clinging to the dust, and this is also called al-daq'a.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿in distress﴾ is one who is cast down on the road, having no house and nothing to shield him from the dust – and in another narration: he is one who clings to the daq'a from poverty and need, having nothing – and in another report from him: he is one far from his homeland.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: That is, the stranger far from his homeland.

Ikrimah said: He is the poor, indebted, needy person.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He is the one who has no one.

Ibn Abbas, Sa'id, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He is the one with dependents.

All of these are close in meaning.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾, meaning: then, along with these beautiful and pure qualities, he is a believer in his heart, seeking the reward of these deeds from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving while he is a believer – those, their striving will be appreciated﴾ [Al-Isra: 19], and He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer﴾ [An-Nahl: 97], to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and enjoined one another to patience and enjoined one another to compassion﴾, meaning: he was among the believers who do righteous deeds, mutually enjoining patience upon the harm of people and compassion towards them. As came in the hadith: "Those who show mercy will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Show mercy to those on earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you." It was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/160) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both. And in another hadith: "He who does not show mercy to people, Allah will not show mercy to him." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2319) from the hadith of Jarir, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Dawud said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ibn Amir – (in another version: Jabir) – from Abdullah ibn Amr, narrating it, who said: "Whoever does not show mercy to our young and does not recognize the right of our elders, is not of us."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those are the companions of the right hand﴾, meaning: those who are characterized by these qualities are among the companions of the right.

Then He said: ﴿But those who disbelieved in Our signs – they are the companions of the left hand﴾, meaning: the companions of the left, ﴿over them will be a fire sealed shut﴾, meaning: closed over them, so there is no escape for them from it and no exit for them from it.

Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Atiyyah al-Awfi, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿sealed shut﴾ means closed over. Ibn Abbas said: "Its doors are closed." Mujahid said: In the language of Quraysh, "asada al-bab" means he closed the door.

A hadith concerning this will come in the surah: ﴿Woe to every slanderer and mocker﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿sealed shut﴾ means a wall with no door.

Qatadah said: "Mu'sadah" means closed shut, so there is no light in it and no opening, and no exit from it ever, forever.

Abu 'Imran al-Jawni said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will command every tyrant, every devil, and everyone who was feared by people in the world for his evil, to be bound in iron. Then they will be driven to Jahannam, and then the gates will be closed upon them, i.e., sealed shut. He said: "By Allah, their feet will never settle on any resting place. By Allah, they will never look out upon the face of the sky from within it. By Allah, the eyelids of their eyes will never meet in a moment of sleep. By Allah, they will never taste cool drink within it, ever." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

End of the commentary on Surah "al-Balad", and all praise and grace are due to Allah.
